AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To quantify the impact of multiyear utilization of preventive dental services on downstream dental care utilization and expenditures for children.

AbstractText.Label: DATA SOURCES/STUDY SETTING
AbstractText.content: We followed 0.93 million Medicaid-enrolled children who were 3-6 years old in 2005 from 2005 to 2011. We used Medicaid claims data of Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Texas.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: We clustered each state's study population into four groups based on utilization of topical fluoride and dental sealants before caries-related treatment using machine learning algorithms. We evaluated utilization rates and expenditures across the four groups and quantified cost savings of preventive care for different levels of penetration.

AbstractText.Label: DATA EXTRACTION METHOD
AbstractText.content: We extracted all dental-related claims using CDT codes.

AbstractText.Label: PRINCIPAL FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: In all states, Medicaid expenditures were much lower for children who received topical fluoride and dental sealants before caries development than for all other children, with a per-member per-year difference ranging from $88 for Alabama to $156 for Mississippi.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The cost savings from topical fluoride and sealants across the six states ranged from $1.1M/year in Mississippi to $12.9M/year in Texas at a 10 percent penetration level. Preventive dental care for children not only improves oral health outcomes but is also cost saving.
